findings.where: First screen, Mark's photograph (desktop and phone), and the 'Graded for the site' image in the Texture section
findings.fault: The lectern photo's backdrop is cut away and replaced with flat slate. What is left is a cut-out head and shoulders pasted onto the ground, with a light fringe along the hair. On desktop the lectern is cropped out, leaving only a microphone at the bottom edge. On phone the dark suit blends into the slate, so a head floats above the heading. The direction was 'Mark at work', with Mark speaking in a real setting and real light. This reads as a studio cut-out instead, with no sign of a talk or an event.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who asked v7 for a full-bleed photo of Mark speaking, real people in real light, and nothing slick. Development-bank staff, who read a keyed cut-out head as cheap and dated rather than as an advisor seen at work.

findings.where: Article specimen, the numbers on the three-item list; the palette table's 'links, the replay control, list numbers' row
findings.fault: The list numbers use the house blue, which the page keeps for links and actions. The specimen's own note says 'blue only where something can be clicked', but nothing happens when these numbers are clicked.
findings.who_objects: A reader of an article, who sees blue numbers next to blue links and the blue PDF control and has to check whether they are links. Angélique, who is given a colour rule that the specimen itself breaks.

findings.where: First screen nav: Profile, Articles and talks, Blog
findings.fault: All three nav items go to the same place, the article specimen, so 'Profile' opens a blog post. The labels 'Articles and talks' and 'Blog' also overlap: the specimen is 'Blog No. 8', and a visitor can't tell which heading an article belongs under.
findings.who_objects: A procurement reader who clicks Profile to check Mark's record and lands in a blog post, and anyone looking for his writing who has to guess between two headings.

findings.where: First screen, 'Mark M. Moseley' at the left of the header, next to the logo
findings.fault: His name is in the top-left spot where a visitor expects the link home, and is styled like the logo next to it. But only the logo is a link; clicking the name does nothing.
findings.who_objects: A visitor on a deep page, such as an article reached from LinkedIn, who clicks the name to go home and gets no response.

findings.fault: The screen says who Mark is and who he advises, but gives no evidence of his work and no regions or places where he has done it. Below it there are only specimens.
findings.who_objects: Staff at development banks who select advisors against terms of reference and look for the kind of work, the region and who asked for it before they write to him.

findings.where: Article specimen, the 'Streamlining the PPP Process' lecture row after the article
findings.fault: One PDF row sits alone after the article with no heading such as 'Related' or 'Talks', so a reader can't tell why it is there. It gives a date but no venue, and its text is indented a few pixels from the article's left edge on both desktop and phone.
findings.who_objects: A reader who finishes the article and can't tell whether this is the article's PDF or a different talk. The founder, for whom the PDF list is the product.

findings.fault: This is a button that replays the animation, but it looks like a prose link: blue and underlined. That look is kept for navigation elsewhere on the page.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who expects to be taken to another page and is not, and the house rule that keeps the link look for navigation.

findings.where: Palette, the text-pair table at phone width
findings.fault: The ratio column is too narrow, so '11.66 : 1' breaks across two lines with the '1' on its own line. The table's figures don't line up.
findings.who_objects: The founder, reading the specimen on a phone, where the broken number looks careless.

findings.where: Texture, the 'Graded for the site' image
findings.fault: Where the cut-out meets the lectern there is a visible diagonal seam in the slate above the lectern's corner. The flat backdrop gives away that it was put in later.
findings.who_objects: The founder, comparing the two images to judge the grade. The seam weakens the claim that the photograph carries the ground.

findings.fault: Neither the nav nor the footer has a 'Contact' item. The hero shows the address, and the footer has it in small type at the far right, but there is no labelled way to get in touch from every page.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who lands on an article and scans the nav for a way to reach Mark.
